_doc: Team ownership graph (separate from job titles). relationship in founder|owner|co-owner|controlling shareholder|chairman|parent company|investor|manufacturer owner. chairman is governance, not ownership. percentage only when a source states it (percentage_note). valid_from/valid_to as precise as the source. Pages show high|medium records only; sources stay here (no per-fact links on pages).

records.notes: Founder of Haas F1 Team (team site: FIA licence granted 2014-04-11). The Race 2026: 'Gene Haas founded the team. Gene Haas controls the team.' No disclosed outside equity investor.
conflicts: Autosport ownership explainer says the team is run and fully owned by Haas Automation (Gene Haas's machine-tool company) rather than Gene Haas personally; The Race cites the Companies House PSC as Gene Haas. Legal holding vehicle unresolved.

records.notes: Team site describes him as 'Founder and chairman, Haas F1 Team' (governance role; ownership recorded separately).

entity.name: Mercedes-Benz Group AG (formerly Daimler AG); holding entity Mercedes-Benz Holdings UK

records.notes: Equal one-third partner since the INEOS deal (down from 60%). Companies House lists Mercedes-Benz Holdings UK as a PSC (per The Race 2026). Autosport: Daimler is now known as the Mercedes-Benz Group.
Joined as a one-third equal shareholder; ultimately Sir Jim Ratcliffe (The Race 2026).

Increased from 30% in the 2020 restructure. Since 2025-11 George Kurtz holds 15% of Wolff's holding company; that company's one-third is unchanged. Wolff is also team principal and CEO (governance, separate).

records.percentage_note: Autosport: Wolff 'purchased a 30% stake' in 2013; Mercedes 2020-12-18: 'Toto Wolff increase his current 30%'.
records.notes: 30% holding from his 2013 arrival until the 2020 INEOS restructure.

records.percentage_note: Mercedes 2020-12-18: 'Daimler will reduce its current 60% shareholding'; Autosport: parent owned the remaining 60% from 2013.
records.notes: 60% majority after the Wolff/Lauda buy-ins of 2013.

records.percentage_note: Autosport: 'non-executive chairman of the board Niki Lauda buying 10%' (2013).
records.notes: Also non-executive chairman (governance). Holding ended after his death in 2019; exact end date and buyer not verified.
conflicts: Autosport says his 10% 'was returned to Mercedes' after he died, but Mercedes/The Race in Dec 2020 still give Daimler 60% and Wolff 30% at that date (10% elsewhere). Unresolved.

records.notes: Full control after buying out Aabar, before the 2013 Wolff/Lauda buy-ins.

records.percentage_note: Autosport 2011-02-28: Daimler 60% / Aabar 40% after buying the remaining 24.9%; Autoweek 2012: 'the 40-percent shareholding that had been held by Aabar'.
records.notes: Bought 30% of Brawn GP alongside Daimler in Nov 2009 (Autosport), rose to 40% in Feb 2011, sold to Daimler in Nov 2012.

records.percentage_note: Autosport: Daimler 'purchased a 45.1% stake in reigning world champions Brawn GP, while Aabar Investments acquired 30%'; Autoweek: Mercedes bought 'a 75.1 percent share' (combined with Aabar).
records.notes: Purchase of 2009 champions Brawn GP, relaunched as Mercedes GP for 2010. Daimler and Aabar moved to 60/40 in Feb 2011.
conflicts: BBC 2009-11-16 says Mercedes would 'buy 75% of Brawn in partnership with an Abu Dhabi investment company'; Autoweek says 75.1% combined.

records.ownership_type: indirect minority investor (15% of Wolff's Motorsport Invest Limited)
records.notes: Indirect stake; team governance unchanged (three one-third holders). Also joined the strategic steering committee as technology advisor.
conflicts: AP headline says Wolff 'sells 15% stake' (reads as 15% of the team); Sky and The Race clarify it is 15% of Wolff's holding entity, about 5% of the team.

records.notes: Scuderia Ferrari sits inside Ferrari itself, not a separate F1 company (The Race); Autosport: Ferrari S.p.A runs its own F1 team. Ferrari N.V. is listed on NYSE and Euronext Milan (RACE).
Agnelli family investment company; loyalty voting shares raise its voting power.
conflicts: Autosport ownership explainer gives an older split: public 67.09%, Exor 22.91%, Piero Ferrari 10%.

records.notes: Holds via a trust; shareholders' agreement with Exor. Also vice chairman (governance, per Autosport).
McLaren Group Limited bought out all McLaren Racing minority shareholders on 2025-09-02 and owns McLaren Racing.

Bought into McLaren in 2007 (Autosport: first held 30%), owned 50% of McLaren Group by Nov 2016 (BBC), full ownership of McLaren Group in Mar 2024 (Autosport), majority shareholder of McLaren Racing alongside CYVN since Sep 2025.
Abu Dhabi investment company; with Mumtalakat holds 100% of McLaren Racing after the minority buy-out.
conflicts: CYVN's non-controlling stake in McLaren Group may date from its Dec 2024 McLaren Automotive deal (not verified from a fetched source); valid_from uses the Sep 2025 McLaren Racing announcement.

records.percentage_note: BBC 2020-12-13: 'initially bought 15% of the firm running McLaren's Formula 1 and IndyCar teams. It will rise to 33%'; BBC 2025-09-02: 'bought a 33% shareholding in McLaren Racing'.
records.notes: 15% initially (Dec 2020) rising to 33% by end of 2022 for GBP185m; bought out in Sep 2025 with O'Connor Capital Solutions funds, Ares and Caspian funds.

records.percentage_note: BBC 2016-11-11: 'Dennis, a 25% shareholder in McLaren Group'. Holding varied over time; 25% is the 2016 figure.
records.notes: Took control after the 1981 Project Four merger and buy-out of original shareholders (Autosport); sold his remaining 25% in 2017 (Autosport).

records.percentage_note: BBC 2016-11-11: 'the remaining 25% owned by Mansour Ojjeh' (Mumtalakat 50%, Dennis 25%).
records.notes: 25% at Nov 2016; start and end dates not verified.

records.percentage_note: Autoweek 2009-11-15: Mercedes 'agreed to sell its 40 percent shareholding in McLaren back to the McLaren Group over the next three years'.
records.notes: Phased sale back to McLaren Group due to complete by 2011, after Daimler bought Brawn. Start date (reported 1999/2000) not verified from a fetched source.
Red Bull GmbH bought Jaguar Racing to create Red Bull Racing (Autosport); at UK level Red Bull Technology sits above the Milton Keynes operation (The Race).
conflicts: Autosport says Jaguar was bought 'in 2005'; a BBC report dated 2004-11-15 (not fetchable) covers the purchase announcement. valid_from uses the first season.

records.ownership_type: ultimate shareholder of parent (Red Bull GmbH)
records.notes: Holds the Mateschitz-side interest in Red Bull GmbH; Companies House lists him at 25-50% of Red Bull Technology (The Race).
conflicts: Autosport: Red Bull GmbH has two shareholders, Chalerm Yoovidhya 51% and Mark Mateschitz 49%. The Race 2026: Mateschitz-side 49%, Yoovidhya-linked TC Agro 49%, Fides Trustees 2% (the 2% moved from Chalerm Yoovidhya personally).

records.ownership_type: ultimate shareholder of parent (Red Bull GmbH)
records.notes: Yoovidhya family interest in Red Bull GmbH.
conflicts: Autosport: Chalerm Yoovidhya 51%; The Race 2026: TC Agro 49% plus Fides Trustees 2%.

records.notes: Red Bull GmbH bought the Minardi team for the 2006 season and renamed it Toro Rosso; AlphaTauri from 2020, RB/Racing Bulls from 2024 (Autosport). Same ultimate shareholders as Red Bull Racing.
conflicts: Minardi purchase completion date (2005) not verified from a fetched source.

records.notes: Red Bull GmbH bought the Minardi team for the 2006 season and renamed it Toro Rosso; AlphaTauri from 2020, RB/Racing Bulls from 2024 (Autosport). Same ultimate shareholders as Red Bull Racing.
Red Bull GmbH bought the Minardi team for the 2006 season and renamed it Toro Rosso; AlphaTauri from 2020, RB/Racing Bulls from 2024 (Autosport). Same ultimate shareholders as Red Bull Racing.

entity.name: Racing Point UK Limited (consortium led by Lawrence Stroll)

records.notes: Bought Force India's business and assets from the administrators in Aug 2018 (FIA): 'the investment consortium led by Lawrence Stroll and the team's senior management'.

The F1 business sits within AMR GP Holdings Limited (The Race); Autosport says Racing Point UK became AMR (GP) Holdings in 2021. Aston Martin Lagonda, the listed road-car company, does not own the team (The Race).
conflicts: Autosport writes 'AMR Holdings GP Limited'; The Race writes 'AMR GP Holdings Limited'.

entity.name: Lawrence Stroll (via Racing Point UK Holdings Limited)

records.notes: Controls the team as 'Controlling Shareholder' under the articles while holding a minority of the economics (The Race). Also executive chairman (governance). Led the 2018 Racing Point consortium.
Bought a minority share in the team's holding company in Nov 2023 (Autosport); The Race calls Arctos 'a substantial shareholder'.

entity.name: Woody Johnson (Robert Wood Johnson, via Green Racer LLC)

records.notes: Minority stake; became Vice Chairman of the team's board (governance) with no day-to-day management role.
Named by The Race as a shareholder; entry date and size not verified.
The Race says PIF 'has an interest'; entry date and size not verified.
Equity interest through a special class of shares; also holds a senior technical role (separate).
US private investment firm; acquired Williams after the strategic review of the then-listed Williams business (The Race). Matthew Savage, Dorilton chairman, chairs Williams (governance).
Co-founded the team with Patrick Head in 1977; family-owned for 43 years until the Dorilton sale (Guardian).
conflicts: Williams was part-listed on the Frankfurt exchange (The Race); 'family-owned' means family-controlled.

records.percentage_note: The Race 2026-09-19: 'Renault Group owns 76% of Alpine Racing Limited.' Autosport: the team sold 24% of its shares in June 2023.
records.notes: Renault ran the Enstone team under its own name until 2021, then as Alpine (Autosport). Its holding before June 2023 is not stated as a number here.

entity.name: Otro Capital-led investor group (incl. RedBird Capital Partners, Maximum Effort Investments)

records.percentage_note: The Race 2026: 'An investor group led by Otro Capital owns 24%'; Autosport: 'sold 24% of its shares to US-based investment group Otro Capital, which includes RedBird Capital Partners and Maximum Effort Investments for just over EUR200m'.
records.notes: EUR200m, valuing Alpine Racing at about $900m (The Race); the group includes athletes and celebrities (e.g. Ryan Reynolds, Patrick Mahomes).
conflicts: The Race 2026 says the saga of the 24% is 'likely to conclude in the coming months' and lists Otro as an 'outgoing Alpine F1 investor'; exit not confirmed from a fetched source.

records.percentage_note: Autosport: 'Audi then acquired a 25% stake in early 2023'.
records.notes: First step of Audi's takeover of Sauber Group ahead of its 2026 works entry.
conflicts: CNBC (2023-01-31, fetch blocked) describes it as a 'minority stake' in the headline.

records.notes: Takeover decision announced Mar 2024 (Audi's QIA release refers to 'the complete takeover of Sauber in March').
conflicts: Completion date of the 100% acquisition (reported Jan 2025) not verified from a fetched source.

records.notes: Audi owns Sauber Holding AG (which runs the Audi F1 team) alongside QIA's significant minority stake.
Definitive agreements signed 2024-11-29 subject to customary regulatory approvals (closing date not verified); signed while the team raced as Kick Sauber.
conflicts: The Race 2026 reports Audi is looking at offers for 33% of the team (via Joe Saward); unconfirmed.

records.notes: GM release 2025-01-09: TWG Motorsports 'in 2024 founded the Cadillac Formula 1 team in partnership with General Motors'. UK company: TWG Cadillac Formula 1 Team Limited.
Leads TWG Global. The Race (2026-09) notes doubt over TWG's long-term involvement after Walter sold other sports assets; TWG denied reports the F1 assets are for sale.
conflicts: Paddock-insider claim (The Race): GM has options up to 30%, Dan Towriss 3%, Walter the rest. Unverified and not recorded as percentages.

records.notes: Founding partner (GM release); per The Race, TWG CEO Dan Towriss has publicly confirmed GM is an equity owner. GM and TWG formed GM Performance Power Units LLC (2025-01-09) for works power units.
conflicts: Public descriptions vary between 'TWG owning the team in partnership with GM' and 'a TWG-owned operation backed by GM' (The Race).

unverified: Haas: whether the legal owner is Gene Haas personally (The Race, Companies House PSC) or Haas Automation (Autosport) is unresolved; no exact % published (only the 75%+ PSC band).
Mercedes: what happened to Niki Lauda's 10% after his death in 2019 (Autosport says returned to Mercedes; Dec 2020 sources still show Daimler 60% / Wolff 30%).
Mercedes: Daimler AG -> Mercedes-Benz Group AG rename only sourced via Autosport wording; no first-party rename release fetched.
Red Bull GmbH ultimate split conflicts (Autosport 51% Yoovidhya / 49% Mateschitz vs The Race 49/49/2 Fides Trustees); recorded without percentages.
Red Bull purchases of Jaguar (BBC, Nov 2004) and Minardi (2005): source pages not fetchable; dates rest on Autosport's summary.

McLaren: Mumtalakat/CYVN split undisclosed; CYVN entry into McLaren Group (Dec 2024 McLaren Automotive deal) and Mumtalakat's Mar 2024 full control only via Autosport/Wikipedia-linked refs not fetched (BBC business-68639320, Reuters).
Aston Martin: % for Stroll (25-50% band), Arctos, HPS, PIF, Woody Johnson and Newey (~4.7% estimate) not disclosed; HPS and PIF entry dates unknown.

Alpine: possible Otro-led group exit (2026) and Mercedes' withdrawn talks over an Alpine minority stake (The Athletic, 2026) not verified; Renault's 2016 purchase of Lotus F1 (renault-2016 id) not sourced here.
Audi: Jan 2025 completion of the 100% Sauber takeover and the QIA closing date not verified; QIA % undisclosed; earlier Sauber owners (Longbow Finance from 2016, per Autosport) not recorded.
Cadillac: exact GM vs TWG/Walter vs Towriss equity split not public; paddock claim (GM options to 30%, Towriss 3%) unverified and not recorded.
Williams: Dorilton's exact holding structure is private (UK company lists no registrable PSC, per The Race); Toto Wolff's former Williams stake (2009) not recorded.
Ferrari: Fiat-era ownership history not recorded (no non-Wikipedia source fetched).
Reuters and AP pages could not be fetched (blocked); AP is cited only for its headline wording in the Kurtz conflict note.
